title: Interface Specification: the CAN transport driver

standards_mappings.reference: Part 6, Clause 8 (software architectural design - interface specification)
standards_mappings.rationale: Specifies the CAN transmit and control boundary with the real signatures, four precondition assertions, the mailbox-exhaustion return contract, the interrupt masking that realises the re-entrancy rule, and the one parameter the source explicitly declines to range-check.
Supplies an interface specification for the CAN transport that the design records' signal tables did not.
Named as the specification the software interface requirements for the communication boundary are derived from.

revision_history.author: sw_engineer
revision_history.description: Four elements of the CAN transport: the transmit call, the 10 ms main function, the periodic-transmit latch and the current-sensor presence read. Two findings are recorded from the source: the identifier value is explicitly not range-checked, by a decision the source documents, and a full transmit mailbox causes the queued-message pump to drop the frame in a branch whose body is empty apart from a comment.

providing_module.name: CAN driver
providing_module.role: Transmits and receives CAN frames for the vehicle network, dispatches received frames to registered callbacks, and runs periodic transmission. It wraps the controller HAL rather than the bus.

consuming_modules.name: 10 ms cyclic task
consuming_modules.consumption_evidence: CAN_MainFunction() at src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.c L266 in the 10 ms cyclic task, and CAN_ReadRxBuffer() at src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.c L255 in the 1 ms cyclic task.

consuming_modules.name: CAN transmit queue pump inside the driver
consuming_modules.consumption_evidence: CAN_SendMessagesFromQueue calls CAN_DataSend(message.canNode, message.id, message.idType, message.data) at src/app/driver/can/can.c L997 and branches on the result at L998.

elements.declaration: extern STD_RETURN_TYPE_e CAN_DataSend(CAN_NODE_s *pNode, uint32_t id, CAN_IDENTIFIER_TYPE_e idType, uint8 *pData);
elements.consuming_module: CAN transmit callbacks and the CAN transmit queue pump

parameters.name: pNode
parameters.unit: node selector (pointer to a configured node)
parameters.meaning: Which of the controller's two CAN nodes the frame goes on.
parameters.valid_range: Either CAN_NODE_1 or CAN_NODE_2, and non-null.
parameters.range_evidence: Two assertions: FAS_ASSERT(pNode != NULL_PTR) at src/app/driver/can/can.c L932 and FAS_ASSERT((pNode == CAN_NODE_1) || (pNode == CAN_NODE_2)) at L936.

parameters.name: id
parameters.meaning: The CAN identifier to put in the frame.
parameters.valid_range: The source states no bound and explicitly declines to assert one. The frame length of the identifier is bounded by the controller, not by this function: an 11-bit identifier is written into bits [28:18] of IF2ARB and a 29-bit identifier into bits [28:0], so the caller must supply a value that fits the width it selected through idType.
parameters.range_evidence: The source records this as a deliberate omission with an AXIVION suppression comment directly above the body: 'id: parameter accepts whole range', at src/app/driver/can/can.c L933.

parameters.name: idType
parameters.meaning: Whether the frame carries an 11-bit standard identifier or a 29-bit extended one.
parameters.range_evidence: FAS_ASSERT((idType == CAN_STANDARD_IDENTIFIER_11_BIT) || (idType == CAN_EXTENDED_IDENTIFIER_29_BIT)) at src/app/driver/can/can.c L934.

values.STD_OK: A free transmit message box was found and canTransmit was called with the frame.
values.STD_NOT_OK: Every one of the CAN_NR_OF_TX_MESSAGE_BOX transmit message boxes was already pending.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: No third value. The single negative condition is mailbox exhaustion, and the return value does not distinguish a full mailbox from a frame the controller refused.
return_contract.evidence: src/app/main/include/fstd_types.h L82-L85. The success assignment is at src/app/driver/can/can.c L968 and the initial value at L938 is returned at L976.

validity_signalling.evidence: STD_OK is assigned only inside the message-box loop after canTransmit, at src/app/driver/can/can.c L968; the value initialised at L938 is returned unchanged at L976 when the loop finds no free box.

timing.evidence: Reached on the 10 ms cycle through the queue pump: CAN_SendMessagesFromQueue calls CAN_DataSend at src/app/driver/can/can.c L997, and CAN_MainFunction, which is called from FTSK_RunUserCodeCyclic10ms at src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.c L266, is the periodic transmit path. FTSK_TASK_CYCLIC_10MS_CYCLE_TIME is 10u at src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.h L112.

concurrency.evidence: Interrupts are disabled around the message-box test and update: portDISABLE_INTERRUPTS() at src/app/driver/can/can.c L946 and the matching portENABLE_INTERRUPTS() at L970 and again at L974, one per loop iteration. The comment at L970 says 'Re-enable interrupts if empty mailbox found' and the one at L974 says 'Re-enable interrupts if all mailboxes are full'.
concurrency.protection_mechanism: Interrupt masking around the mailbox search and update, released on every loop iteration.

error_paths.condition: pNode is NULL or is neither CAN_NODE_1 nor CAN_NODE_2.
error_paths.observed_behaviour: A precondition assertion trips before the loop.

error_paths.condition: idType is neither of the two defined identifier widths.
error_paths.observed_behaviour: A precondition assertion trips before the loop.
A precondition assertion trips before the loop.

error_paths.condition: id holds a value too wide for the selected identifier length.
error_paths.observed_behaviour: No check is performed. The value is shifted into IF2ARB and the excess bits are lost or corrupt a neighbouring field; the source records this as a deliberate non-assert.
error_paths.evidence: src/app/driver/can/can.c L933 records that the parameter accepts the whole range, and L953-L966 shift the value without masking.

error_paths.condition: All CAN_NR_OF_TX_MESSAGE_BOX transmit message boxes are already pending.
error_paths.observed_behaviour: The loop runs to completion, the frame is not sent, and STD_NOT_OK is returned.
error_paths.evidence: src/app/driver/can/can.c L945 loop bound, L947 mailbox test, L975 and L976 return

not_specified_by_source: The interface does not state the maximum payload length. It takes a bare uint8 * and passes it to canTransmit, so the frame length is whatever the caller wrote into it and this interface does not check it. The receive path declares CAN_DEFAULT_DLC, so a reader could wrongly assume a matching bound here.
The interface does not state which mailbox a frame was placed in, so a caller cannot correlate a transmit mailbox interrupt with the frame it sent.
The interface does not state whether a frame handed to it is still valid after the call returns. The pointer is read during the call and not retained here, but nothing says so.

The identifier value is not range-checked at all, by explicit decision recorded in the source. A requirement that the interface shall reject an out-of-range identifier is not satisfiable against this implementation.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: Not applicable as a return value; the function reports nothing.

validity_signalling.mechanism: None returned. It advances internal timing and optionally transmits.
validity_signalling.evidence: Declared void at src/app/driver/can/can.h L112; the body at src/app/driver/can/can.c L1008-L1013 calls CAN_CheckCanTiming and, conditionally, CAN_PeriodicTransmit.

timing.evidence: Called from FTSK_RunUserCodeCyclic10ms at src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.c L266; FTSK_TASK_CYCLIC_10MS_CYCLE_TIME is 10u at src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.h L112.

concurrency.evidence: Called from the 10 ms cyclic task at src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.c L266, whose priority is FTSK_TASK_CYCLIC_10MS_PRIORITY = OS_PRIORITY_HIGH at src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.h L106. The CAN interrupt handlers are separate entry points in the same file and do not reach this one.

error_paths.observed_behaviour: Only the timing check runs; CAN_PeriodicTransmit is not called.
error_paths.evidence: src/app/driver/can/can.c L1010 tests can_state.periodicEnable against true

not_specified_by_source: The interface does not state that periodic transmit is gated on a separate enabling call. A caller that never calls CAN_EnablePeriodic gets timing checks only, with no indication that periodic frames are suppressed, because the gate is a static read of internal state.

The interface states no relationship between the 10 ms call period and the configured period of any individual message. Those periods are configuration validated elsewhere by TEST_CAN_ValidateConfiguredTxMessagePeriod, not by this interface.
The interface returns nothing, so a caller cannot tell whether the timing check found a problem.
The interface does not say what it does when it is called at a period other than 10 ms. The 10 ms figure is imposed by the task, not by this interface.

parameters.name: command
parameters.meaning: Whether periodic CAN transmission is enabled.
parameters.valid_range: true or false; the parameter is a bool, so no other value is representable.
parameters.range_evidence: The declaration's parameter type is bool at src/app/driver/can/can.h L136.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: Not applicable as a return value, and the absence of a return matters here: the call sets a latch that CAN_MainFunction reads later, and the interface gives the caller no way to read the latch back or to confirm the change.
return_contract.evidence: Declared void at src/app/driver/can/can.h L136; the body writes can_state.periodicEnable at src/app/driver/can/can.c L1035 and L1037.

validity_signalling.mechanism: None returned. The element writes one internal flag.

timing.evidence: Called once from the system state machine at src/app/engine/sys/sys.c L452 as CAN_EnablePeriodic(true), not on a period.

concurrency.evidence: Called from src/app/engine/sys/sys.c L452, which runs in the state-machine trigger, not in an interrupt context.

error_paths.observed_behaviour: No error path exists; the function writes the flag and returns.

not_specified_by_source: The interface does not state the initial value of the flag. A reader cannot tell from the header whether periodic transmission starts enabled or disabled.
The interface does not state when the change takes effect relative to the next CAN_MainFunction call, so the ordering requirement between this element and the periodic task is undocumented.

The interface provides no read-back, so a caller that sets the flag cannot confirm it took effect. The set of CAN_IsCurrentSensorPresent-style readers covers the sensor-presence flags but not this one.
The interface does not say what periodic transmission means: which frames, at which periods. Those are configuration, not interface.

elements.consuming_module: BMS state machine and application code

parameters.name: stringNumber
parameters.meaning: The string whose current-sensor presence is asked for.
parameters.range_evidence: FAS_ASSERT(stringNumber < BS_NR_OF_STRINGS) at src/app/driver/can/can.c L1042. BS_NR_OF_STRINGS is (1u) at src/app/application/config/battery_system_cfg.h L109.

values.true: The driver has recorded that a current sensor is present on that string.
values.false: The driver has not recorded one, which is also the value before any sensor has been seen.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: The default is not distinguished from an observed absence: the array is a static boolean and its zero value is indistinguishable from a sensor that was never found.
return_contract.evidence: Declared with a doxygen comment at src/app/driver/can/can.h L136-L142; the body returns can_state.currentSensorPresent[stringNumber] at src/app/driver/can/can.c L1043.

validity_signalling.evidence: The element returns bool, so the caller can read the recorded state.

timing.evidence: Read on demand by application code rather than periodically. The flag it returns is written by the transmit configuration, so its freshness is not tied to any period this interface states.

concurrency.evidence: Called from application code in src/app/application; no interrupt context reaches it in the source. The write side and the read side are not shown to be mutually excluded.

error_paths.condition: stringNumber is at or above BS_NR_OF_STRINGS.
error_paths.observed_behaviour: A precondition assertion trips before the read.

not_specified_by_source: The interface does not state how currentSensorPresent is set, by which message, or on what evidence. The setter in the same file is a test hook, TEST_CAN_SetCurrentSensorPresent, so the production path that establishes presence is not identified by this interface.

The interface cannot distinguish 'no sensor' from 'sensor not yet detected', because both are false. A requirement that the interface shall report absence reliably is not satisfiable against this implementation without a further statement about detection timing.
The interface does not state a staleness bound on the value it returns, so a caller cannot tell a fresh reading from a stale flag.

interface_level_gaps.gap: A queued frame is silently discarded when the retransmit queue is full.
interface_level_gaps.consequence: The transmit path has no back-pressure signal to its caller. A frame queued for retransmission is dropped without a diagnosis event, a return value or a log, so a communication requirement about guaranteed delivery cannot be traced to this interface.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: At src/app/driver/can/can.c L997-L1003, CAN_DataSend returning STD_NOT_OK causes the message to be re-queued with a zero timeout, and if that re-queue fails the branch body is empty apart from the comment 'Queue is full.'.

interface_level_gaps.gap: The identifier value is not range-checked, by explicit decision.
interface_level_gaps.consequence: An identifier wider than the selected frame length is not rejected and not reported; it is shifted into the controller register and the excess bits are lost. The interface's own error contract therefore has a hole that the source documents rather than closes.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: src/app/driver/can/can.c L933 records 'id: parameter accepts whole range' with an AXIVION suppression, and L953-L966 shift id into IF2ARB with no mask.

interface_level_gaps.gap: The transmit interface and the receive dispatch are two unrelated halves with no shared contract.
interface_level_gaps.consequence: The receive side registers callbacks by node, identifier and identifier width and dispatches in CAN_ReadRxBuffer, while the transmit side takes the same triple. Nothing in the interface states that the two must agree, and there is no shared registration record that both sides read, so a mismatch between a transmitted and an expected identifier is a runtime dispatch failure rather than a configuration error.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: Transmit takes pNode, id and idType at src/app/driver/can/can.h L101; receive dispatch matches canNode, id and idType against the configured table in src/app/driver/can/can.c L1019-L1027.

interface_level_gaps.gap: The interface never states the arbitration or bus-level contract: no bit rate, no identifier allocation, no maximum frame rate.
interface_level_gaps.consequence: No requirement about CAN behaviour can be traced into this interface. The bit rate is configuration and the identifier allocation is spread across the transmit callback files, neither of which this interface names.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: The header declares only function prototypes and the constant CAN_NR_OF_TX_MESSAGE_BOX (32u) at src/app/driver/can/can.h L72.

verification_status.statement: The contract above was read from the source at the pinned commit and has not been compared with what the code does when it runs. Every behavioural statement is a reading of the implementation text, not an observation of behaviour. Where the two could differ, this record does not know.
